title: Software repository
summary: A software repository, or repo, is a storage location for software packages, often including a table of contents and metadata. Repositories are typically managed via source or version control and repository managers. Publishers or organizations host these servers on the Internet, either freely or by subscription, and may focus on specific languages or entire operating systems. Operators provide package management systems to search for, install, and manipulate packages. Major repositories aim to be malware-free, especially when using digitally signed repositories from reputable vendors combined with appropriate permissions systems. Most Linux distributions maintain many mirrored repositories worldwide. Package managers help users install from and update repositories, managing dependencies between packages.

mechanisms.title: Storage and Metadata Organization
mechanisms.explanation: A repository functions as a storage location for software packages, typically maintaining a table of contents and associated metadata to organize the packages available for installation.

mechanisms.title: Package Manager Integration
mechanisms.explanation: Package managers facilitate the integration of code from different sources into a coherent operating unit, allowing users to automatically install and update repositories and manage dependencies between packages.
